title: Brownian continuum random tree limits of finite Fortuin–Kasteleyn maps above four
main_claim: For fixed q>4, an n-edge critical FK planar map with graph distance scaled by c(q)n^{-1/2} and the normalized degree measure converges in GHP to the Brownian CRT (T_e, d_e, mu_e), through all n. The proof uses an exact word identity, then strict drift and ladder cuts to get a square-root lower bound on the coefficients, then a critical finite-variance block Galton–Watson tree with 2n+1 nodes, then a uniform law of large numbers for marked paths under only a second moment, and finally pole/LCA distance and corner-mass comparisons.

issues.description: The joint limit of the Lukasiewicz walk and the height process for conditioned finite-variance GW trees, through all attainable sizes, is imported from Broutin–Marckert (Theorem 3, Lemma 11, Section 6). Its hypotheses are paraphrased but not restated, and the reduction from random degree counts to fixed ones (subsequence plus dominated convergence) is only sketched. This is standard and I believe it is correct.
issues.evidence: Proof of Prop. tree:excursion cites BM14 Thm 3 and Lemma 11. The normalizations W/(sigma sqrt N) and sigma H/(2 sqrt N) agree with the standard Aldous/Marckert–Mokkadem normalizations.

coverage:
I read the whole paper (words, ladders, blocks, trees, metric, about 1900 lines).

Checked by computation:
- Brute-force check of the word identity P(empty-reducing)=a_n u^n for n<=4 at p=1/3 (t=1), where a_n = 2^n × #rooted maps because T(2,2)=2^|E|: values 4, 36, 432, 6048 all match.
- At p=3/4 the identity gives a_1=2x and a_2=8x^2+2x with x=1+t, matching a hand enumeration of the 9 rooted 2-edge maps.
- b_1=2(1+t), and b_2=14=T(digon) from the block equation.
- Flexible/fixed ratio 2p/(1-p)=t, and u=(1-p)/16.

Checked by hand:
- Strict-drift proof: optional stopping, the covariance bound E[T D^(m)] >= 2E[K; J<=m], and the variance increment 1-pE[TD] (conditional mean of a flexible letter is -(p/2)T). The resulting EK<=1/(2p) is consistent with Sheffield's EK=(1-p)/p.
- L-cut positivity via shortened pieces and Wald's identity.
- R-cut: Green density 2r for the reversed scan, the remainder density (1-S)1{max<=0}, and the escape probability 1-EK.
- Bottom-supply/terminal-demand matching lemma, including its case analysis.
- Uniform seam success, including small k<=D.
- Coefficient lower bound by counting intervals: (2n-1) intervals of length 2n through the seam.
- Quadratic inverse criterion: f'=(Phi-2yPhi')/Phi^3, the secant bound forcing f'(v)=0, and the f'' argument for Phi''(v)<infinity.
- Offspring mean 1 and variance 1+4v^2Phi''/Phi.
- Exact finite law Phi^{-N} v^n a(M).
- Otter–Dwass formula and the span-2 local limit constant.
- Spine means E(K-I)=sigma^2/2 and EK=E xi^2.
- Union bound for bounded labels (pi_N^{-1} ~ N^{3/2} against e^{-c sqrt N}), and truncation using only a second moment.
- LCA walk-minimum lemma.
- Additivity of pole distances across cut vertices, with error at most 2Delta.
- Corner-to-degree pushforward.
- Constant c(q)=nu/(sqrt2 beta sigma)=sigma/(2 sqrt2 beta).
- GHP correspondence lemma.

Not checked line by line: the cited Broutin–Marckert theorem itself, and the full bijective tour argument (only spot-checked numerically, as above).
sibling_notes: Family 211 siblings: q=4 critical sphere, subcritical conformal/metric, linear clock, FK-Ising spectral. All are no_gap_found and partial, with each one's worst point resting on its companion papers. This paper states that the companions are context only and not inputs. I confirmed that it is self-contained: none of its steps uses a companion result.
